correctness.rationale: Exact substitution of positive payoffs gives xdot=x(1-x)(e-gY) and a composition-independent logistic Lotka–Volterra P,Y subsystem. The strict Lyapunov identity Vdot=-(P-P*)²/K plus LaSalle gives global P,Y convergence. Direct differentiation proves the exact first integral at c=0 and drift identity at all parameters; logarithmic odds then yield the sharp selected-prey classification. At neutrality, Jacobian has one tangent zero and two strictly stable eigenvalues; every positive trajectory converges to a uniquely given equilibrium. All nonstandard symbolic cancellations are replayed by the included standalone checker; experiments cannot substitute for the global Lyapunov proof.

value.rationale: Balanced antisymmetric off-diagonal payoff contrasts are motivated by measuring individual ecological selection while keeping aggregate birth and capture rates fixed: the predator community follows the same logistic ecological dynamics at every composition but prey fitness differs. The theorem pinpoints a nontrivial global selection threshold, proves a normally attracting interval of biological equilibria at equal long-run fitness, and quantifies irreversible environmental-memory effects on final composition by exact explicit power laws. This is a natural structural dynamical classification, not arbitrary numerical parameter slicing or a generic textbook linearization.
